BUS.G12.T2.CSR.A1.title: Social responsibility, CSR & CSI
BUS.G12.T2.CSR.A1.description: Critically examining social responsibility and its implications for business and communities: Corporate Social Responsibility (nature, process, benefits, challenges, components) and Corporate Social Investment (nature, projects, responsible business practice), and meaningfully contributing time and effort to others' well-being.
BUS.G12.T2.CSR.A1.strand: T2 — CSR, human rights, teams, sector & environment, leadership & quality
BUS.G12.T2.CSR.A1.recovery_strategy: CSR = the whole responsible way a business operates (ethics, environment, health and safety). CSI = the specific projects and money a business invests in communities (a part of CSR). Both go beyond what the law requires.

questions.question: What do the letters 'CSR' stand for?
questions.memo: CSR is Corporate Social Responsibility — a business operating responsibly towards society and the environment.

questions.question: What do the letters 'CSI' stand for?
questions.memo: CSI is Corporate Social Investment — the specific projects and resources a business invests in communities.

questions.question: True or false: Corporate Social Responsibility goes beyond what the law strictly requires.
questions.memo: CSR is voluntary responsibility beyond the legal minimum — giving back to society and protecting the environment.

questions.question: Funding and running a community school project is an example of corporate social _________.
questions.memo: Specific community projects a business funds, like a school, are Corporate Social Investment (CSI).

questions.question: True or false: CSR can benefit both the business and the community.
questions.memo: Done well, CSR helps the community and also builds the business's reputation, staff morale and customer goodwill.

questions.question: CSR includes caring for the _________, for example by reducing pollution.
questions.memo: Protecting the environment — reducing pollution and waste — is one component of CSR.

questions.question: Sort each example into CSR (broad responsible practice) or CSI (a specific community project).

items.text: Building a clinic for a township
Treating all staff and suppliers fairly
Operating safely and ethically as standard

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: CSR is the overall responsible way of operating; CSI is the specific projects and investments in communities.

questions.question: What is the difference between CSR and CSI?
options: CSR is the overall responsible way a business operates; CSI is the specific community projects it invests in
CSR is illegal; CSI is legal
CSR is only about profit; CSI is only about tax
They are exactly the same thing
questions.expected: CSR is the overall responsible way a business operates; CSI is the specific community projects it invests in
questions.memo: CSR is the broad responsibility; CSI is the concrete investment in projects — CSI is one part of CSR.

questions.question: Thesis: 'A profitable business should invest some of its resources in its community.' Choose the THREE strongest supporting reasons.
questions.thesis: A profitable business should invest some of its resources in its community.

pool.text: It helps address real social needs like education and health
It builds goodwill and a strong reputation
A healthier, more skilled community provides better customers and workers
Investing in the community always bankrupts a business
The CEO enjoys cutting ribbons at events
It is only worth doing if it is legally forced

questions.memo: The strong reasons are meeting real needs, building goodwill, and a stronger community of customers and workers. The others are false, irrelevant or miss the voluntary nature of CSR.

questions.question: A key benefit of CSR to a business is an improved _________.
questions.memo: Visible responsibility improves a business's reputation, which helps attract customers, staff and partners.

questions.question: What is a challenge of CSR for a business?
options: It costs money and time that must be balanced against other needs
It always makes an instant profit with no cost
It is completely free to run
questions.expected: It costs money and time that must be balanced against other needs
questions.memo: CSR requires real resources — money, time and effort — which the business must balance against its other priorities.

questions.question: True or false: CSI projects can help address human-rights issues in a community.
questions.memo: CSI projects — such as supporting education, health or access for people with disabilities — can advance human rights in a community.

questions.question: Sort each outcome into whether it mainly benefits the business or the community.
questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Reputation, loyalty and morale mainly benefit the business; schooling, a cleaner environment and jobs mainly benefit the community — though the two often overlap.

questions.question: Which of these is a component of CSR?
options: Caring for the environment, health and safety, and acting ethically
questions.expected: Caring for the environment, health and safety, and acting ethically
questions.memo: CSR components include environmental care, health and safety, and ethical conduct.

questions.question: What does responsible business practice involve over the longer term?
options: Meeting the longer-term needs of the society in which the business operates
Focusing only on this month's profit
questions.expected: Meeting the longer-term needs of the society in which the business operates
questions.memo: Responsible business practice considers the long-term well-being of society, not just immediate profit.

questions.question: Meaningfully contributing _________ and effort helps advance the well-being of others.
questions.memo: Giving time and effort — not only money — is part of contributing meaningfully to others' well-being.

questions.question: A company wants its CSI to make a real, lasting difference. Which project fits best?
options: A skills-training centre that helps locals find lasting employment
A one-off photo opportunity with no follow-up
A donation announced loudly but never paid
A project that benefits only the executives
questions.expected: A skills-training centre that helps locals find lasting employment
questions.memo: Lasting CSI builds capacity — like a skills centre — rather than one-off gestures that fade quickly.

questions.question: How should one critically evaluate CSR that is used mainly for publicity?
options: Genuine CSR creates real, lasting benefit; CSR used only for image risks being seen as 'window-dressing'
Publicity is the only purpose of CSR
questions.expected: Genuine CSR creates real, lasting benefit; CSR used only for image risks being seen as 'window-dressing'
questions.memo: CSR should be judged by real impact; doing it only for publicity, without lasting benefit, can backfire as hollow 'window-dressing'.

questions.question: Why can CSR support a business's long-term success, not just its image?
options: A healthier, more skilled, more stable community provides better customers, workers and operating conditions
Because CSR removes the need to make any profit
Because society has no link to business
questions.expected: A healthier, more skilled, more stable community provides better customers, workers and operating conditions
questions.memo: Investing in the community strengthens the very base of customers, workers and conditions the business depends on for long-term success.

questions.question: How are CSR and CSI best understood together?
options: CSI (specific community projects) is one way a business puts its broader CSR into practice
CSR and CSI have nothing in common
CSR is only for charities and CSI only for governments
questions.expected: CSI (specific community projects) is one way a business puts its broader CSR into practice
questions.memo: CSR is the broad responsibility; CSI is a concrete part of it — the projects through which a business acts on that responsibility.
